The newly emerged juvenile possesses a minute shell measuring just 0.08 centimeters [Lb = 0.08 centimeters] in length at birth, a dimension that reflects the substantial yolk reserves allocated to the developing embryo. Field surveys commonly report this settlement event as a key bottleneck for recruitment success, with juvenile survivorship heavily influenced by the availability of suitable biofilm-covered surfaces in flowing waters.

Before the onset of independent feeding, the newly formed juvenile relies entirely on its endogenous yolk reserves.
